Suitable phase reversing, motor-operated, air-break disconnect switches would be provided to accomplish phase reversal as required for reverse rotation of the generator-motors.
A switchyard would be located adjacent to the transformer bank, from which a 1,600-foot long section of overhead 525-kV transmission line would lead to the proposed location of a future 525-kV tie station.
A 525-kV transmission line would then extend 7.67 miles in a general southerly direction to a juncture with the Applicant's existing Jocassee-Oconee 230-kV transmission line and would utilize 9.19 miles of the existing transmission line right-of-way. The last segment of the transmission line, a 1.04 mile section, would lead from the existing Jocassee-Oconee right-of-way to the Applicant's Oconee Nuclear Plant. The proposed transmission line right-of-way is depicted by Figure 1-9.
The new right-of-way would be 200 feet wide. The 525-kV line would be supported by steel lattice, single-circuit towers varying from 96 to 176 feet in height. The towers would be located 1,000 to 1,500 feet apart and would vary from 28 to 68 feet square at the tower base. Minimum wire clearance at any point would be 45 feet to the ground.
The transmission line would cross 2 major State highways, S. C. 11 and S. C. 183, and 1 major waterway, Lake Keowee. Six secondary roads and 10 small streams would also be traversed.
An alternative right-of-way, located slightly to the west of the proposed right-of-way, was considered for that section of the transmission line leading from the location of the proposed future tie station to the existing Jocassee-Oconee transmission line right-of-way. Both the proposed and the alternative routes are considered to be viable and each follows the mountainous terrain and topography as much as possible to to minimize visual impact and the amount of required clearing. The route nearest Lake Jocassee (7.67 miles) is the Applicant's preferred route, because it is shorter than the alternative (8.17 miles).
